## Addressing Modes (names and syntax)

| Abbrev | Name | Operand Syntax | Example |
|---|---|---|---|
| `A` | Accumulator | `A` or omitted | `ASL A` / `ASL` |
| `#` | Immediate | `#byte` | `LDA #$0F` |
| `ZP` | Zeropage | `$LL` | `LDA $00` |
| `ZPX` | Zeropage,X | `$LL,X` | `LDA $10,X` |
| `ZPY` | Zeropage,Y | `$LL,Y` | `LDX $10,Y` |
| `ABS` | Absolute | `$HHLL` | `LDA $C000` |
| `ABSX` | Absolute,X | `$HHLL,X` | `LDA $D000,X` |
| `ABSY` | Absolute,Y | `$HHLL,Y` | `LDA $D000,Y` |
| `IND` | Indirect | `($HHLL)` | `JMP ($FFFC)` |
| `IZX` | (ZP,X) | `($LL,X)` | `LDA ($40,X)` |
| `IZY` | (ZP),Y | `($LL),Y` | `LDA ($40),Y` |
| `REL` | Relative | label | `BEQ done` |
| `IMP` | Implied | — | `CLC` |

*6510 `JMP (addr)` has the classic page‑wrap bug at `$xxFF → $xx00`.*

records.name: data/basic/basic-spec.md
records.text:
<!-- Source: data/basic/basic-spec.md#2.1 System Pointers (Zero Page) -->
### 2.1 System Pointers (Zero Page)

| Name | Address | Meaning |
|------|----------|----------|
| **TXTTAB** | `$002B–002C` | Start of BASIC text (default `$0801`) |
| **VARTAB** | `$002D–002E` | Start of variable table |
| **ARYTAB** | `$002F–0030` | Start of array storage |
| **STREND** | `$0031–0032` | End of arrays (+1) |
| **FRETOP** | `$0033–0034` | Bottom of string storage |
| **MEMSIZ** | `$0037–0038` | Highest BASIC RAM address |

Variables grow upward from `TXTTAB`; strings grow downward from `MEMSIZ`.  
`ARYTAB` always follows `VARTAB`; defining new scalars after arrays shifts array memory upward by 7 bytes per variable.

---

records.name: data/basic/rom-routines.md
records.text:
<!-- Source: data/basic/rom-routines.md#Compact Workflows -->
## Compact Workflows

| Need | Preferred mechanism | Minimal sequence |
|:--|:--|:--|
| Evaluate expression | `FRMNUM`/`FRMEVL` | Set `TXTPTR` to first char, `JSR $AD8A` or `JSR $AD9E`, handle BASIC errors. |
| Numeric result as text | `FOUT` | FAC1 ready, `JSR $BDDD`, copy A/Y string immediately. |
| Parse byte/address syntax | `GETBYT`/`GETADR`/`GETNUM` | Use BASIC-compatible expression text and controlled `TXTPTR`. |
| Read/write numeric scalar | `PTRGET` + `MOVFM`/`MOVMF` | Set `TXTPTR` to var name; use returned `VARPNT`. |
| Install tokenized program | Raw write + `LNKPRG` + `CLR` | Write at `TXTTAB`, final next pointer `$0000`, `JSR $A533`, `JSR $A65E`. |
| Execute BASIC statement | Dynamic keyboard or normal interpreter | Avoid direct statement entries unless runtime/error context is controlled. |
| Reserve high RAM | Lower `MEMSIZ`, then `CLR` | Update `$37/$38`, `JSR $A65E`; keep ML/sprites above new top. |

records.text:
<!-- Source: data/basic/rom-routines.md#Avoid as General MCP APIs -->
## Avoid as General MCP APIs

| Entry | Reason |
|:--|:--|
| `$A437` | BASIC error path; non-returning for normal callers. |
| `$A7AE` | Main interpreter loop; full runtime context required. |
| `$A7ED` | Command dispatcher; token/stack conventions required. |
| `$E206` | May skip a return address at end-of-statement. |
| `$E37B`, `$E394` | Warm/cold BASIC entry paths, not subroutines. |
| Direct string allocation/GC | Safe only when descriptor stack and movable string heap are controlled. |

records.name: data/drive/drive-spec.md
records.text:
<!-- Source: data/drive/drive-spec.md#Assembly Examples -->
### Assembly Examples

#### Print Directory

```asm
    lda #<dir
    ldx #>dir
    ldy #len
    jsr $ffbd   ; SETNAM
    lda #1      ; logical
    ldx #8      ; device
    ldy #0      ; secondary
    jsr $ffba   ; SETLFS
    jsr $ffd5   ; LOAD (LOAD"$",8)
dir: .text "$"
len = *-dir
```

#### Load File

```asm
    lda #<name
    ldx #>name
    ldy #len
    jsr $ffbd
    lda #0      ; LFN=0
    ldx #8      ; device
    ldy #1      ; SA=1
    jsr $ffba
    lda #0
    jsr $ffd5   ; LOAD (A=0=load)
name: .text "HELLO.PRG"
len = *-name
```

#### Save File

```asm
    lda #<name
    ldx #>name
    ldy #len
    jsr $ffbd
    lda #0
    ldx #8
    ldy #1
    jsr $ffba
    lda #0
    jsr $ffd8   ; SAVE
name: .text "HELLO.PRG"
len = *-name
```

---

records.name: data/gamedev/techniques.md
records.text:
<!-- Source: data/gamedev/techniques.md#3. Smooth scrolling -->
## 3. Smooth scrolling
- Hardware fine scroll: `$D016` bits 0-2 (X), `$D011` bits 0-2 (Y). Use 38-column mode (`$D016` bit 3 = 0) and 24-row mode (`$D011` bit 3 = 0) so new data enters under the border.
- Horizontal loop: fine X goes 7 down to 0 (scrolling left); when it wraps, shift screen RAM left by one character and set X back to 7 (or reverse). Keep the new column prepared in advance from the tile map (a 2x2 or 4x4 character metatile per map cell).
- Double-buffer screen RAM (two screens at `$C000`/`$C400`, flip `$D018` and sprite pointers on the wrap). Do the shift in parts across the 8 fine steps (for example 3 rows per frame) so no frame overruns. Cost: an unrolled `lda abs,x / sta abs,x` copy is about 9 cycles per byte; one full screen (960-1000 bytes) is ~9,000 cycles.
- Colour RAM problem: colour RAM `$D800` is a single copy and cannot be double-buffered or re-pointed. Options: (a) use one colour per tile type and a charset where colour comes from the character (multicolour chars with colour 8-15, same colour for the whole map region); (b) copy colour RAM row-wise just behind the raster beam; (c) shift colour RAM in the same split steps while the fine-scroll hides the seam; (d) use a bitmap mode and draw colour into screen RAM instead. Pick (a) when the art allows it.
- Vertical: same with `$D011` and a row shift; changing Y scroll moves the badline, which disturbs stable-raster code.
- Parallax: split the screen with raster IRQs and set different `$D016` values per band; far bands scroll slower (every 2nd or 4th frame). Multicolour text mode: OR bit 4 (`$10`) into the `$D016` value.
- HUD: bottom or top band with its own `$D016`/`$D018` set at a raster IRQ.
- MODERN: turbo can do the full shift in the frame; a world map can live in REU and deliver one new column or row per frame (one 256-byte fetch). `c64://ultimate/reu`. Upic scrolls by re-pointing byte columns (2 pixels per step), see `c64://ultimate/upic`.
**Seen in:** Corescape and Oscar64 `hscrollshmup` (character-mode parallax, two screens, 8 px fine scroll), Tony (flip-screen alternative, no scroll), Upic projects (ring buffer scroll).

records.name: data/gamedev/techniques.md
records.text:
<!-- Source: data/gamedev/techniques.md#7. Random numbers -->
## 7. Random numbers
```
rnd:    lda seed          ; 8-bit Galois LFSR, period 255; seed must not be 0
        asl
        bcc +
        eor #$1d
+       sta seed
        rts
```
- Seed from something unpredictable at the first fire press: `$D012` XOR a free-running CIA timer low byte, or the frame counter when the player pressed a key.
- SID noise as a hardware source: voice 3 frequency `$D40E/$D40F = $FFFF`, control `$D412 = $80` (noise, gate off), read `$D41B` (voice 3 oscillator). Voice 3 then cannot play music; mute it in the mix.
**Seen in:** common practice; CIA/SID sources recommended in `c64://io/cia/spec`, `c64://sound/sid/spec`.

records.name: data/graphics/sprite-charset-best-practices.md
records.text:
<!-- Source: data/graphics/sprite-charset-best-practices.md#Character Definition Format -->
### Character Definition Format

Each character uses 8 bytes (8 rows × 8 pixels):

```text
Byte 0: Row 0 bitmap (MSB = leftmost pixel)
Byte 1: Row 1 bitmap
...
Byte 7: Row 7 bitmap
```

Example: 'A' character

```text
00111100  ($3C) - Row 0
01100110  ($66) - Row 1
01100110  ($66) - Row 2
01111110  ($7E) - Row 3
01100110  ($66) - Row 4
01100110  ($66) - Row 5
01100110  ($66) - Row 6
00000000  ($00) - Row 7
```

records.name: data/graphics/sprite-charset-best-practices.md
records.text:
<!-- Source: data/graphics/sprite-charset-best-practices.md#Charset Memory Alignment -->
### Charset Memory Alignment

Custom charsets must be aligned to 2KB boundaries:

- `$2000` (8192) - VIC bank 0, offset $0000
- `$2800` (10240) - VIC bank 0, offset $0800
- `$3000` (12288) - VIC bank 0, offset $1000
- `$3800` (14336) - VIC bank 0, offset $1800

records.text:
<!-- Source: data/graphics/vic-spec.md#VIC View -->
### VIC View

| Bank | CPU Range | VIC Range | Contents |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 0 | $0000-$3FFF | $0000-$3FFF | RAM; char ROM at $1000-$1FFF. |
| 1 | $4000-$7FFF | $0000-$3FFF | RAM. |
| 2 | $8000-$BFFF | $0000-$3FFF | RAM; char ROM at $1000-$1FFF. |
| 3 | $C000-$FFFF | $0000-$3FFF | RAM. |

- CIA2 port A bits 0-1 (inverted) choose the active 16 KB bank.
- Colour RAM (10-bit address) appears as upper nybble on every VIC read regardless of bank.

records.name: data/graphics/vic-spec.md
records.text:
<!-- Source: data/graphics/vic-spec.md#Character ROM -->
## Character ROM

The **Character ROM** (*chargen*) for the C64 is **4 KB at $D000–$DFFF (53248–57343)**, consisting of **two 2 KB sets** (each 256×8-byte glyphs):

- **Set 1 (uppercase/graphics):** $D000–$D7FF (53248–55295), 256 entries
- **Set 2 (lowercase/uppercase):** $D800–$DFFF (55296–57343), 256 entries

**Screen codes** index glyphs; **PETSCII codes** are logical character codes used by BASIC/KERNAL. Screen memory at **$0400–$07E7** stores screen codes that the **VIC-II** uses to fetch 8-byte bitmaps from the active character set.

records.name: data/graphics/vic-spec.md
records.text:
<!-- Source: data/graphics/vic-spec.md#Graphics Modes (ECM/BMM/MCM) -->
## Graphics Modes (ECM/BMM/MCM)

Graphics mode is selected by the following bits in $d011 and $d016:

- `ECM` (bit 6 of $d011): Extended Colour Mode.
- `BMM` (bit 5 of $d011): Bit Map Mode.
- `MCM` (bit 4 of $d016): Multi Colour Mode.

| Mode | Bits (ECM/BMM/MCM) | Memory interpretation | Pixel output |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Standard text | 0/0/0 | `c`: char code + colour nybble; `g`: CB bits + RC | 8x8 pixels; bit 1 uses `c[11:8]`, bit 0 uses B0C ($d021$). |
| Multicolour text | 0/0/1 | `c[11]` selects multi flag | Flag 0: standard text; flag 1: 4x8 pixels, 00->B0C, 01->B1C, 10->B2C, 11->`c[10:8]`. |
| Standard bitmap | 0/1/0 | `c`: foreground/background nybbles; `g`: bitmap byte | 8x8 pixels; bit 0 -> `c[3:0]`, bit 1 -> `c[7:4]`. |
| Multicolour bitmap | 0/1/1 | `c`: colours for 01/10/11 | 4x8 pixels; 00->B0C, 01->`c[7:4]`, 10->`c[3:0]`, 11->`c[11:8]`. |
| ECM text | 1/0/0 | Upper char bits select B0C..B3C (char set reduced to 64) | Foreground uses `c[11:8]`; background chosen via `c[7:6]`. |
| Invalid text | 1/0/1 | Same addressing as ECM multi; outputs black | Useful for collision tricks; no visible pixels. |
| Invalid bitmap 1 | 1/1/0 | Bitmap with A9/A10 forced low | Displays black; repeats sections; collisions still occur. |
| Invalid bitmap 2 | 1/1/1 | Multicolour bitmap with A9/A10 forced low | Black output; collisions possible; 4x8 grouping. |
| Idle state | any (when sequencer idle) | `g` fetch at $3fff/$39ff, video matrix treated as zero | Outputs backgrounds per mode (typically B0C or black). |

records.name: data/io/cia-spec.md
records.text:
<!-- Source: data/io/cia-spec.md#CIA #2 Registers (`$DD00–$DD0F`) — IEC/User Port/RS‑232/VIC Bank/NMI -->
## CIA #2 Registers (`$DD00–$DD0F`) — IEC/User Port/RS‑232/VIC Bank/NMI

| Address | Decimal | Name | Function / Bits (compact) |
|:-------:|:-------:|:-----|:---------------------------|
| `$DD00` | 56576 | **PRA** | **IEC** + **VIC bank** + RS‑232 TXD. **b7** DATA IN, **b6** CLOCK IN, **b5** DATA OUT, **b4** CLOCK OUT, **b3** ATN OUT (bus lines active‑low via drivers); **b2** RS‑232 TXD (user M); **b1..b0** VIC 16 KiB bank: `00=$C000–FFFF`, `01=$8000–BFFF`, `10=$4000–7FFF`, `11=$0000–3FFF` (power‑on `11`). |
| `$DD01` | 56577 | **PRB** | **User Port/RS‑232** lines (TTL). **b7** DSR (L), **b6** CTS (K), **b5** User‑J, **b4** DCD (H), **b3** RI (F), **b2** DTR (E), **b1** RTS (D), **b0** RXD (C). **Also:** PB7/PB6 timer outputs when enabled. |
| `$DD02` | 56578 | **DDRA** | Port A direction. Default `$3F` (b6–b7 in). |
| `$DD03` | 56579 | **DDRB** | Port B direction. Default `$00`; RS‑232 may set b1–b2 out when opened. |
| `$DD04` | 56580 | **TALO** | Timer A low (R counter / W latch low). |
| `$DD05` | 56581 | **TAHI** | Timer A high (R counter / W latch high). |
| `$DD06` | 56582 | **TBLO** | Timer B low. |
| `$DD07` | 56583 | **TBHI** | Timer B high. |
| `$DD08` | 56584 | **TOD10TH** | TOD tenths BCD. (OS typically unused here.) |
| `$DD09` | 56585 | **TODSEC** | TOD seconds BCD. |
| `$DD0A` | 56586 | **TODMIN** | TOD minutes BCD. |
| `$DD0B` | 56587 | **TODHR** | TOD hours BCD + AM/PM (b7). |
| `$DD0C` | 56588 | **SDR** | Serial shift data (rarely used by OS; available via user port SP2/CNT2). |
| `$DD0D` | 56589 | **ICR** | As CIA1, but flags drive **/NMI**. **b4**=FLAG (user‑port pin B). |
| `$DD0E` | 56590 | **CRA** | As CIA1 `$DC0E`. |
| `$DD0F` | 56591 | **CRB** | As CIA1 `$DC0F`. |

**Notes (CIA2):** Provides **IEC** master control (ATN/CLOCK/DATA), **User Port** digital I/O and RS‑232 signals, and **VIC bank** selection via `PRA[1:0]`. `/PC2` (handshake) pulses low for one cycle after **PRB** access—available on user port for external strobing.

## SID ($D400-$D41C)

- Voices 1-3: freq ($D400/$01, $D407/$08, $D40E/$0F), pulse width ($D402-$D403 etc.), control ($D404,$D40B,$D412), ADSR ($D405-$D406 etc.).

## Miscellaneous

- $DE00-$DFFF: Reserved expansion I/O.
- Sprite pointers: `$07F8-$07FF`, value × 64 (+ bank) gives sprite data address.
- To map sprite 0 to `$02C0`: `POKE 1024+1016,11` (pointer 11 ⇒ `$02C0`).
- Colour RAM: `$D800-$DBFF`, lower nybble only.

---

This layout keeps the essential Commodore 64 addresses compact for LLM consumption while retaining full coverage of the supplied map.

## Register Map (base = $D400 / 54272)

**Per Voice (1 – 3):**

| Function | Voice 1 | Voice 2 | Voice 3 | Bits / Notes |
|-----------|----------|----------|----------|--------------|
| Frequency LO | $D400 | $D407 | $D40E | Low byte of 16-bit pitch increment |
| Frequency HI | $D401 | $D408 | $D40F | High byte |
| Pulse Width LO | $D402 | $D409 | $D410 | 12-bit value (0-4095) |
| Pulse Width HI | $D403 | $D40A | $D411 | Upper 4 bits used |
| Control | $D404 | $D40B | $D412 | **7..0 = NOISE PULSE SAW TRI TEST RING SYNC GATE** |
| AD | $D405 | $D40C | $D413 | Attack/Decay nibbles |
| SR | $D406 | $D40D | $D414 | Sustain/Release nibbles |

**Global:**

| Function | Address | Description |
|-----------|----------|-------------|
| Cutoff LO | $D415 | Lower 8 bits of filter cutoff |
| Cutoff HI | $D416 | Upper 3 bits of cutoff |
| Res/Routing | $D417 | 7..4 = resonance (0–15); 3..0 = route Ext,V3,V2,V1 into filter |
| Mode/Volume | $D418 | 0..3 = master vol (0–15); 4..6 = LP/BP/HP; 7 = CH3 off |
| Read-backs | $D419–$D41C | POTX, POTY, OSC3, ENV3 |

## Typical Usage Snippet (ASM)

```asm
; Initialize SID
lda #$0f        ; volume = 15
sta $d418

; Play note (Voice 1 example)
lda freq_lo
sta $d400
lda freq_hi
sta $d401
lda #$00
sta $d402
lda #$08
sta $d403
lda #$11
sta $d405
lda #$f3
sta $d406
lda #%01000001  ; pulse + gate
sta $d404

; ... release ...
and #%11111110
sta $d404
```

records.name: data/ultimate/hardware.md
records.text:
<!-- Source: data/ultimate/hardware.md#Multiple SIDs -->
## Multiple SIDs

- Two UltiSID (FPGA) plus two physical sockets (SID Socket 1/2; user-accessible sockets on the C64U are unverified). Items: `SID Socket 1/2 Address`, `UltiSID 1/2 Address`.
- Address options: `Unmapped`, `$D400`..`$D7E0` in steps of `$20`, `$DE00`..`$DEE0`, `$DF00`..`$DFE0` (steps of `$20`). Default: all four at `$D400`.
- `Auto Address Mirroring` (default Enabled) mirrors the available SIDs over all of `$D400-$D7FF`. A write to "the second SID" at `$D420` can hit the same chip on a mono setup. Real stereo needs distinct addresses and distinct panning.
- Range split (`UltiSID Range Split`, up to 8 SIDs / 24 voices): `1/2 (A5)` second half at +`$20`, A6 +`$40`, A7 +`$80`, A8 +`$100`; `1/4 (A5,A6)`, `(A5,A8)`, `(A7,A8)`. Both UltiSIDs share the split. Sockets: `Ext DualSID Range Split` Off, A5..A9.
- SIDs at `$DE00`/`$DF00` collide with REU, UCI, Ultimate Audio and ACIA (how the core arbitrates is unverified).
- Per UltiSID (config only, not C64-visible): filter curve (8580 Lo/Hi, 6581, 6581 Alt, U2 Low/Mid/High), resonance, combined waveforms 6581/8580, digi level Off/Low/Medium/High. Analog behaviour is user-selectable; do not rely on exact 6581/8580 digi level.
- Mixer (volume, panning per source) affects HDMI/analog out only. A running built-in SID player may override the SID config (`SID Player Autoconfig`).
- Detection: no Ultimate-specific SID count register for C64 code. Use ordinary SID probing at each candidate base (see c64://sound/sid/spec), bounded. Deprecated UCI GET_HWINFO sub 1 lists configured SID bases (c64://ultimate/uci). Host side: REST `GET /v1/configs/SID Addressing` and `SID Sockets Configuration`.

records.name: data/ultimate/hardware.md
records.text:
<!-- Source: data/ultimate/hardware.md#I/O area `$DE00-$DFFF` -->
## I/O area `$DE00-$DFFF`

| Range | Device |
|---|---|
| `$DF00-$DF0A` | REU (1750 set; Ultimate extras at `$DF0C-$DF0F` unverified on U64 cores); see c64://ultimate/reu |
| `$DF1B-$DF1F` | UCI; see c64://ultimate/uci |
| `$DF20-$DFFF` | Ultimate Audio sampler, only if `Map Ultimate Audio $DF20-DFFF` enabled (default Disabled); register layout not verified here |
| `$DE00`/`$DF00`/`$DF80` (+1 NMI variant) | ACIA 6551 SwiftLink, when `ACIA (6551) Mapping` is not Off (DE00/IRQ, DE00/NMI, DF00/IRQ, DF00/NMI, DF80/IRQ, DF80/NMI) |
| `$DE00-$DFE0` | optional SID placements |

- An active REU disables cartridges that need `$DF00-$DFFF` (EasyFlash, Final Cartridge III). A loaded .crt makes the internal cartridge own `$DE00-$DFFF`; REU/UCI/Audio/ACIA availability then is unverified.
- ACIA "turbo" (Turbo232 register) is modem baud, unrelated to CPU turbo.
- RTC: read it through UCI DOS GET_TIME; there are no memory-mapped RTC registers.

records.name: data/ultimate/reu.md
records.text:
<!-- Source: data/ultimate/reu.md#Routine (ca65 syntax, fresh example) -->
## Routine (ca65 syntax, fresh example)

```
REU_STAT = $DF00
REU_CMD  = $DF01
REU_C64  = $DF02        ; lo, hi
REU_ADDR = $DF04        ; lo, mid, bank
REU_LEN  = $DF07        ; lo, hi
REU_IRQM = $DF09
REU_CTRL = $DF0A
; zp: c64p (2), reup (3), lenp (2), cmd (1)
reu_do:
        php
        sei
        lda c64p
        sta REU_C64
        lda c64p+1
        sta REU_C64+1
        lda reup
        sta REU_ADDR
        lda reup+1
        sta REU_ADDR+1
        lda reup+2
        sta REU_ADDR+2
        lda lenp
        sta REU_LEN
        lda lenp+1
        sta REU_LEN+1
        lda #0
        sta REU_IRQM
        sta REU_CTRL
        lda cmd                 ; $90 stash, $91 fetch, $92 swap, $93 verify
        sta REU_CMD             ; MUST be the last register write
        nop
        nop
        plp
        rts
```
- In C compilers (Oscar64 reordered stores to constant I/O addresses once) write the register sequence as one inline-assembly block, and re-read the first byte of a fetched buffer through a volatile pointer.

records.name: data/ultimate/reu.md
records.text:
<!-- Source: data/ultimate/reu.md#Pitfalls -->
## Pitfalls

1. REU disabled by default; size default 2 MB.
2. Stale or absent REU looks like valid data: magic, version, checksum at boot.
3. Preload is boot-only; use LOAD_REU or a stub for reproducible loads.
4. Command register last; no compiler reordering.
5. Split DMAs at 512 KB boundaries; length 0 means 64 KB.
6. Autoload restores base values, so use no-autoload for streaming consecutive blocks.
7. `$DF0A` fix bits persist: clear them after use.
8. `$FF00` mode leaves a pending command until `$FF00` is written; a stray store starts it.
9. Reading `$DF00` clears flags and IRQ; enabling the REU IRQ requires reading it in the handler.
10. VICE charges DMA at about 1 cycle per byte (3.10, measured); Ultimate rates differ: test streaming budgets on hardware.
11. GeoRAM mode replaces the REU (window `$DE00`, banks `$DFFE/$DFFF`; layout unverified).

records.name: data/ultimate/upic.md
records.text:
<!-- Source: data/ultimate/upic.md#Display model -->
## Display model

- 384x256 pixels = 192 "byte columns" x 256 rows. Column c holds pixel x = 2c in the low nybble and x = 2c+1 in the high nybble, row = offset inside the column (column-major, 256 bytes per column, 49,152 bytes). Same as Upic `.upic` files.
- Pixel address: `col_base(x >> 1) + y`; even x = low nybble mask `$0F`, odd x = high nybble mask `$F0`.
- The buffer is ordinary C64 RAM (default `$1000-$CFFF`). Common layout: first 8 columns relocated to `$E000` (under KERNAL, needs `$01 = $35`), the rest at `$1800 + (c-8)*256`, generated renderer page-aligned at `$E800` up. Code gets only about 6-7 KB resident; large programs need REU overlays.
- A bare 49,152-byte bitmap or v1.3 `.upic` file (256-byte header "Upic1.3" + `$AE`, size fields, text, 48-byte palette at `$D0`, bitmap at `$100`) holds pictures; older converters write a separate `.pal`.
- There is no framebuffer register, blitter or double buffer. Pixels are written by CPU stores, REU DMA or UCI DMA loads into the columns. A second 48 KB buffer does not fit in RAM.
- Palette: pixel values are VIC colour indices 0-15 written to `$D020`; their RGB comes from the Ultimate palette (UCI `04 51-54`). A palette change recolours the whole display at once with no pixel redraw.

records.name: sid-overview.md
records.text:
# SID Quick Reference (for RAG)

See `data/sound/sid-spec.md` for the full guide. This stub ensures the RAG index includes SID guidance.

- Base address: $D400
- Voice control: $D404/$D40B/$D412 (bits: NOISE PULSE SAW TRI TEST RING SYNC GATE)
- Play note: set FREQ LO/HI, PW LO/HI, AD, SR; set CTRL with waveform|GATE
- Stop note: clear GATE bit in CTRL
- Volume/filter: $D418 (bits 0..3 volume, 4..6 LP/BP/HP)
- Filter cutoff: $D415/$D416 (11 bits)
- Useful effects: arpeggio (rewrite FREQ), vibrato (modulate FREQ), PWM (modulate PW), filter sweeps ($D415/$D416)
